title: Top 7 Document Upload Rejection Reasons across Indian Exams & Portals
metaDescription: Discover the top 7 reasons why UPSC, NSP, SSC, JoSAA, and State PSC portals reject document uploads. Fix file size caps, invalid file formats, blurry text, and password protection.
author: Zcompressor Engineering
heroHeadline: Common document upload rejection reasons & how to fix them.
heroDescription: Document rejections during government scholarship and exam registrations can cost candidates their application eligibility. Here are the top 7 failure modes and how to prevent them.

sections.heading: 1. Exceeding exact file size ceilings (KB / MB limit).
body: Portals like NSP (200 KB), UPSC (300 KB), and SSC strictly enforce hard file size limits. Uploading a 205 KB PDF to a 200 KB portal ceiling triggers automated backend validation errors.

sections.heading: 2. Password-protected or encrypted PDF files.
body: Government document verification bots cannot open PDFs protected with user passwords or restricted editing permissions. Ensure your PDF is unencrypted before uploading.

sections.heading: 3. Wrong file format extension (.JPG uploaded as .PDF or vice versa).
body: Uploading a JPEG file renamed manually to '.pdf' will fail MIME-type server checks. Always use a proper document converter or native PDF export.

sections.heading: 4. Blurry or illegible official seals & Roll Numbers.
body: Over-compressing an image to an extreme low resolution can smudge Tehsildar seals, QR codes, or marksheet Roll Numbers, resulting in manual verification rejection.

sections.heading: 5. Document size below minimum KB threshold.
body: Portals like UPSC require documents to be at least 20 KB (between 20 KB and 300 KB). Compressing a 1-page text file down to 12 KB will cause a 'file too small' validation error.

faq.q: How can I test if my compressed PDF is acceptable before submitting?
faq.a: Open the compressed PDF in your device PDF viewer, zoom in to 100%, and verify that your Roll Number, Name, and seals are clear and unencrypted.
